area: hazel-jit: a pattern by position against a labeled tuple of unknown type answers where the interpreter is stuck
text: Found checking ^ticket(847)'s decision 3. `let f = fun r -> let (a, b) = r in a - b in f((x = 5, y = 2))`: the interpreter binds a to the labeled entry (x = 5) and its subtraction is stuck (an indeterminate BinOp); the jit (Hazel.jit, hazeljs at a97b6f7465) answers 3, since compiled code reads the pattern as r[0], r[1]. The same with f declared (Int, Int) -> Int. When the matched type is labeled, the statics add the labels to the pattern (MatchedTyp.prod) and compiled code reads r["x"], so only an unknown or unlabeled matched type meets this. Fix: a positional read in compiled code checks that the entry at that position is unlabeled, and an indeterminate run ($R.indet) goes to the interpreter, as hazel-jit's rule has it; then an agreement test for it (evaluator sweep or the jit's own). With records as objects (847), the same check is Array.isArray.
